content: Opuntia ficus-indica, commonly known as prickly pear cactus, has been studied for its potential hypoglycemic effects in patients with Type 2 diabetes. However, there is insufficient evidence to support its use for managing benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and further research is required in this area. Opuntia ficus-indica has been shown to enhance the effects of several antidiabetic medications through pharmacodynamic synergism. These medications include acarbose, glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, regular human insulin, metformin, miglitol, nateglinide, pioglitazone, repaglinide, rosiglitazone, saxagliptin, sitagliptin, and vildagliptin. Due to this interaction, it is recommended to use caution and closely monitor patients when combining Opuntia ficus-indica with these medications, as the risk of hypoglycemia may increase. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, the safety profile of Opuntia ficus-indica is not well established. While the roots of the plant may not work effectively when consumed with high-fiber foods, there is no significant evidence of fetal risk based on controlled studies in pregnant women. However, its pregnancy category is listed as NA (not applicable), and its safety during lactation remains unknown. Therefore, caution is advised when considering its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
